findings.explanation: With no type definitions and one identifier, Lean returns the same `ARB` for every starting stamp. It therefore equates the results for starting stamps 0 and 1. HOL4 gives equations only for two empty lists and for two nonempty lists. Its equations allow these two mismatched calls to return different lists.
findings.repair:
private axiom type_def_to_ctMap_unspecified {α β γ : Type} :
  Namespace mlstring mlstring (List mlstring × typ) → Nat →
  List (α × β × List (mlstring × List ast_t)) → List γ →
  List (stamp × α × List typ × γ)

noncomputable def type_def_to_ctMap {α β γ : Type}
    (tenvT : Namespace mlstring mlstring (List mlstring × typ)) :
    Nat → List (α × β × List (mlstring × List ast_t)) → List γ →
      List (stamp × α × List typ × γ)
  | _, [], [] => []
  | next_stamp, (tvs, _, ctors) :: tds, id :: ids =>
    type_def_to_ctMap tenvT (next_stamp + 1) tds ids ++
    List.reverse (ctors.map fun (cn, ts) =>
      (.TypeStamp cn next_stamp, (tvs, ts.map (type_name_subst tenvT), id)))
  | next_stamp, tds, ids => type_def_to_ctMap_unspecified tenvT next_stamp tds ids
findings.lean_check:
import CmlTS.TypeSysProps
open CmlTS

example (env : Namespace mlstring mlstring (List mlstring × typ)) :
    type_def_to_ctMap (α := Unit) (β := Unit) env 0 [] [()] =
    type_def_to_ctMap (α := Unit) (β := Unit) env 1 [] [()] := by
  simp [type_def_to_ctMap]
